correctness.rationale: For positive parameters \(a,b,t,x\) with \(t=1-a\), direct substitution gives the exact identity \(V\circ F-V=(c-c_*)/t-\Phi(x/x_*)\); literal SymPy cancellation reproduced. The function \(\Phi\) is nonnegative and vanishes only at unit normalized activation. For compact sets \(F(K)=K\), every point has a bounded full history. If \(c<c_*\), backward values of \(V\) increase without bound on any positive full orbit, contradicting the compact upper bound. On the axis, the only bounded full orbit is the resting point. In compact positive stationary states, sufficiently small positive activation is a one-way geometric sink; recurrence excludes those states almost surely and proves integrability of \(\log x\), allowing stationary integration. At \(c=c_*\), zero defect forces \(x=x_*\) and then \(y=x_*-\log x_*\), with a separate axis-contraction case. Above threshold the integrated identity gives the exact expectation and Markov concentration. The fixed-point fold follows by strict convexity of \(qx-t\log x\). Symbolic checks are finite algebraic certificates, never substitutes for proofs about infinite dynamics.

originality.rationale: The fold and two positive equilibria are explicitly published in the 1993 Chialvo working paper and are excluded from the novelty claim. The new theorem provides an exact zero-bias log-potential coboundary implying exclusion of all nonzero compact full orbits strictly below the known fold, exactly classifies compact stationary measures on the fold, and enforces a KL-type quantitative activation budget on every compact positive invariant probability measure above it. Unlike local equilibrium and finite-resolution results, these are all-invariant-set and all-invariant-measure statements for every admissible positive triple. A same-system 2006 article was only available as an abstract; no independence or exhaustive absence is claimed.

value.rationale: The 1993 map was built to distinguish transient excitability from autonomous recurrent spiking. For a noninvertible two-coordinate neuronal map, nonexistence of a positive fixed point alone does not exclude non-fixed recurrent compact sets. The log-recovery potential now gives a complete compact recurrence exclusion below the previously known fold, a two-equilibrium stationary rigidity result at the boundary, and an exact quantitative activity budget for arbitrary compact stationary states above it. The latter supplies an invariant test and concentration estimate for any periodic or chaotic regimes at zero input. It is a structural, parameter-global result, not a routine fixed-point substitution, a numerical increment, or a known table recomputation.
